summary.text: Kweisi Mfume is the Democratic incumbent in Maryland's 7th Congressional District. A Baltimore native, he served on the Baltimore City Council and in the U.S. House from 1987 to 1996, led the NAACP for nine years, and returned to Congress by winning a 2020 special election. He advanced from the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 70.1% of the vote.

paragraphs.text: Mfume was born, raised and educated in Baltimore, according to his congressional biography.

He graduated magna cum laude from Morgan State University, where he later taught as an adjunct professor, and earned a master's degree in liberal arts with a concentration in international studies from Johns Hopkins University.
Before winning his first election, Mfume worked as an activist, radio commentator, administrator and television personality.
He won a seat on the Baltimore City Council at age 31 and served on it from 1978 to 1986, chairing its Committee on Health Policy.

He then represented Maryland's 7th District in the U.S. House from 1987 to 1996; his official biography lists service on the Banking and Financial Services, Education, Small Business and Ethics committees, and chairmanships of the Joint Economic Committee and the Congressional Black Caucus.
Mfume left Congress in February 1996 to become president and chief executive officer of the NAACP, a post he held for nine years.

According to his official biography, he was later executive director of the National Medical Association (from 2010) and led a National Institutes of Health-funded health policy research consortium in Maryland from 2013 to 2018.
Mfume was sworn in on May 5, 2020, after winning a special election to fill the term vacated by the death of Rep. Elijah Cummings, and has since been elected to full terms.

He serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, where he is ranking member of the Government Operations Subcommittee, and on the Committee on Foreign Affairs. He also chairs the Morgan State University Board of Regents.
